picks.thesis: Textbook convergence. Four House members (Fields, Cisneros, Allen, Letlow) disclosed TSM buys Jan-May 2026, and eleven TSM executives — including Chairman/CEO Wei Che-Chia — made open-market, non-10b5-1 purchases on 2026-06-05 (lag ~4d), with VP Yuan adding on 2026-06-22. Congress plus broad, fresh insider buying that runs from the CEO through the VP ranks is the strongest pattern in this dossier. Bands are modest and the congressional legs are older, but insider breadth is the anchor. Shares are down 6.5% over 30 days, roughly 17% below the 90-day high (477.57) and near the 90-day low (365.38).
key_risks: Congressional buys are small ($1-15k bands) and up to five months stale
Insider buys, though open-market, are clustered on a single date (2026-06-05), limiting them as independent signals
Price is near its 90-day low, so buying has not yet marked a bottom
picks.invalidation: TSM executives begin filing open-market sales, or the June insider buyers do not add, while price breaks below the 90-day low of 365.38.

picks.thesis: Convergence with a repeat congressional buyer. Rep. David Taylor (House Agriculture; Transportation & Infrastructure) accumulated IBP across four disclosed buys from Jan to Jun 2026 (latest 2026-06-15, lag 16), while four insiders — Director Hilsheimer, COO Wheeler, CFO Miller and Chief Admin Niswonger — made open-market, non-10b5-1 purchases on 2026-05-11 and 2026-06-11 (lag 1-4). One persistent congressional buyer plus a four-person insider cluster is genuine two-family convergence. Caveats: the congressional leg is a single filer and bands are small ($1-15k). Shares are up ~5% over 30 days, well below the 90-day high of 313.80.
key_risks: Congressional conviction rests on one member (Taylor)
Insider buys are two-plus months old
picks.invalidation: The four insiders reverse to sales, or Taylor files an IBP sale, with no new open-market buying appearing.

key_risks: Price near the 90-day high leaves little downside cushion
Insider buys, while sizable, are two members
picks.invalidation: Aguzin or Melamud file MELI sales, or Cisneros stops adding, while price rolls over from the 90-day high.

picks.thesis: Eleven QNT insiders recorded open-market, non-10b5-1 purchases — including Directors Barron (~$15.0M) and Jimenez (~$4.0M), CSO Dehoff and CFO Sharan — alongside one small congressional buy by Rep. Cleo Fields (2026-06-04, $1-15k). The dollar breadth is striking, but every insider purchase carries the identical 2026-06-05 date, so it most likely reflects a single event rather than eleven independent conviction signals, and the congressional leg is one small filer. Shares fell ~20% over five days and sit near the 90-day low (51.40). Treat the size with caution given the single-date caveat.
key_risks: All insider buys share one date, so they may be one financing/directed event rather than independent signals
Congressional support is a single small filer
Price is sliding hard toward the 90-day low
picks.invalidation: The one-date insider buyers file sales, or no follow-on buying on independent dates appears while price breaks the 90-day low of 51.40.

picks.thesis: Fresh multi-member cluster. Three members bought AT&T within weeks in June 2026 — Rep. Tim Moore at a $50-100k band (2026-06-04, lag 1), Rep. David Taylor (2026-06-05, lag 7) and Sen. Gary Peters (Armed Services; Commerce) (2026-06-29, lag 3). A low-lag, three-member cluster with one sizable band is the next-strongest pattern after convergence, but there is no insider confirmation and no committee-sector alignment. Shares are down 4.6% over 30 days, near the 90-day low (20.21).
key_risks: Cluster signal only — no insider or committee confirmation
Two of the three bands are small ($1-15k)
picks.invalidation: The three-member cluster reverses to disclosed sales, or fails to broaden, while price breaks below the 90-day low.

picks.thesis: Top of the engine's ranking on committee alignment alone. Rep. Dan Newhouse (Appropriations; Select Committee on the CCP) bought on 2026-07-10 (filed 2026-07-17, lag 7) and Rep. Maria Salazar (Foreign Affairs; Financial Services) bought $15-50k on 2026-03-24, both flagged as aerospace/defense-aligned overseers. Two members buying is a modest signal and the Newhouse leg is fresh, but this rests on committee alignment with no insider confirmation, and Salazar's leg is nearly four months old and small. Shares are down 6.5% over 30 days, near the 90-day low (215.92). Note that oversight alignment is also why such trades draw scrutiny.
key_risks: Single signal family (committee), no insider buying
Salazar's buy is stale and small; Newhouse's is small
Committee-sector alignment is the entire thesis
picks.invalidation: Newhouse or Salazar file HON sales, or no further committee-aligned buying appears while price breaks the 90-day low.
